title: Shooting victim had dark side, mourners told during funeral
article: --- Andrew Moore, who was shot dead by police last Friday, was a "tender and generous man" whose life became wrapped up in the drug trade, leading to his tragic death, an overflow crowd heard at his funeral Wednesday.
"Andy was a loving father and friend, an avid fisherman, avid hunter and avid golfer," said a friend of Moore's, who introduced himself as Roy.
He recalled the time he and Moore took their sons to a Blades hockey game. It was the first time Moore's boy, Dylan, watched a live game.

"Andy wasn't sure if Dylan would understand it, but when the home team scored, Dylan raised his hands and cheered. Andy's face lit up like the proudest dad," Roy told the crowd, which consisted of many leather-clad bikers wearing vests and skull caps.
Roy himself wore a black T-shirt with a red cross and the words, West Coast Choppers on it.
"But Andy also had a shadowy side. He got pulled into drugs and drawn away from his family and friends. It was drugs that resulted in the situation that led to Andy's death," Roy said.
Several frames holding collages of photographs from Moore's life were on display at the Park Funeral Chapel, with crying mourners gathered around.

None of the bikers had patches indicating they were part of an organized group, but there were plenty of Harley-Davidson patches about. Moore's funeral card included an image of the Harley logo inside.
The 35-year-old Moore died from a single gunshot wound the head at about 6:20 p.m. Friday after a confrontation with a veteran Saskatoon police constable.
The scuffle took place inside the Twenty-Ninth Street Confectionery, into which Moore ran in an attempt to escape the pursuing officer.

Moore was well-known to the constable from previous encounters, police officials have said. The media has been told that two warrants were issued against Moore -- for dangerous driving and obstructing a police officer -- but police did not elaborate.

A check with the provincial courthouse revealed that three warrants were issued on the same day, March 7. The third cited Moore for operating a motor vehicle while being pursued by police "in order to evade the peace officer."
His obstruction charge was for refusing to provide an officer with required information pertaining to a driving offence then turning away, getting back into his car and driving away.

The officer who shot Moore had tried arresting him for the outstanding warrants moments earlier on the street. Moore made a bid to run through the confectionery but was halted by a locked rear door. According to police, he pulled out a loaded large-calibre handgun and ignored three warnings to drop it. The officer shot when the gun was pointed his way, police officials have said.

Police have not released the name of the officer, who has 10 years of experience, according to Chief Russell Sabo. Police are reluctant to release much details about the situation, waiting instead for an expected inquest to bring it out.
